input: Draft a LinkedIn recommendation for a colleague

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The colleague's role, industry, and relationship to the writer shapes every detail — what skills to highlight, the right framing, and the level of authority the recommender can speak to.

Knowing which specific skills, projects, or accomplishments to feature determines the substance and focus of the recommendation — a broad character endorsement reads very differently from a project-specific one.
The working relationship (manager, peer, direct report, client) defines the credibility angle and what the writer can authentically vouch for.
Whether the recommendation is meant to help land a new job, gain visibility, or support a promotion changes the tone, emphasis, and persuasive angle needed.
The desired tone — warm and personal vs. formal and professional — directly affects word choice, structure, and how much storytelling vs. fact-listing to include.
Length is a real constraint on LinkedIn; knowing if there is a target length or word count prevents writing something too short to be compelling or too long to be read.
Understanding whether the colleague has given any guidance, a draft, or bullet points to work from — or whether this is starting from scratch — determines the immediate first step.

gold.taskTitle: Draft a LinkedIn recommendation for a colleague
gold.taskDescription: Write a compelling LinkedIn recommendation for a colleague that accurately reflects their strengths and contributions.

questions.title: What is your colleague's job title and industry?
questions.description: Knowing their role and field shapes the vocabulary, credibility framing, and which qualities matter most to highlight.

questions.title: What specific skills or achievements should be highlighted?
questions.description: Identifying standout accomplishments or strengths gives the recommendation concrete, memorable substance beyond generic praise.

questions.title: What was your working relationship with this colleague?
questions.description: Whether you were their manager, peer, direct report, or client determines the angle of authority and what you can authentically vouch for.

questions.title: What is the primary purpose of this recommendation right now?
questions.description: A recommendation aimed at a job search, a promotion, or general professional visibility each requires a different persuasive focus.

questions.title: Should the tone be warm and personal or formal and professional?
questions.description: Tone determines the entire voice of the piece — from heartfelt storytelling to concise, polished endorsement.

questions.title: Do you have a target length or word count in mind?
questions.description: LinkedIn recommendations typically range from 75 to 300 words; knowing the target prevents writing something too brief or too lengthy.

questions.title: Do you have any notes or bullet points to work from already?
questions.description: Knowing whether raw material exists — or if this starts from scratch — sets the immediate first step for drafting.
